text: The case state, the case move, the committee queue item, the open deviation and its handler route, and the WO rule package are consumed on their owners' published contracts, never as tables or views, and their operation names stay placeholders until the owners publish them.
why: Only rwb-case writes recovery_case and the queue, only rwb-deviation writes the deviation facts, and only rwb-decision governs the rule rows and the ledger. The legacy Data table names recovery_case, deviation, queue, decision_log_entry and rule_row, none of which is this service's, while TSD S7 T5.2 names published interfaces only as module interfaces and publishes no operation name for the move, the queue item, the deviation route or the package read, so no name may be invented. The plan's C and X rows are empty, so these rows are class C in fact and not in the metadata.

text: write_off.decision_log_id is written with the identifier the local decision-record library returns, and the P7 ledger entry identifier is not stored on the write-off row; the ledger entry itself is written by rwb-decision on the shared decision-record topic.
why: DF-FIN-012 is described as 'the decision_log_entry this record belongs to' and decision_log_entry is P7's table, while DP-03 keeps a local record in the caller's transaction and P7 keeps the central ledger. Storing a foreign identifier the service cannot verify would be a value it cannot maintain, so the column carries the record this service writes and the ledger stays with its owner.
